title: The back-to-back tax, measured in the box score
headline_insight: On the second night of a back-to-back, NBA per-36 box-composite production dips about 0.315 versus rested games (13.591 vs 13.905) -- small, but it stacks with schedule compression.
what_it_means: Fatigue shows up in the box score but modestly at the player level: the raw pooled per-36 penalty is -0.315 for a back-to-back, -0.217 for 3-games-in-4-days, and -0.193 for 4-in-6. These lenses overlap, so their counts do not add up -- a back-to-back that closes a cluster is also a 3-in-4.
how_to_read: The rested baseline is games with >= 2 days rest and no compression; each density class shows its pooled per-36 mean and the delta beneath the baseline.
why_it_matters: The significance-tested version of this effect lives in a separate receipt: -1.73 pts/100 team ORtg (rested minus back-to-back), n 4732, p 0.0056 -- so the descriptive dip here is the player-level footprint of a team effect that clears a real test.
caveat: DESCRIPTIVE_ONLY, edge_claimed false; raw pooled per-36 means, NOT roster/opponent/minutes/home-away adjusted and NOT significance-tested in this module; overlapping classes are not additive.

cited.value: -1.73 pts/100 team ORtg (rested minus b2b), n=4732, p=0.0056

as_of: unknown (artifact carries no as_of field); seasons pooled 2023-24, 2024-25, 2025-26
